approved: Customs Amendment (Immediate Destruction of Illicit Tobacco) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would allow customs officials to destroy seized illicit tobacco products immediately instead of storing them for 30 days.
The Comptroller-General of Customs would be given the power to decide how to handle tobacco products seized as prohibited imports from 1 July 2019, including immediate destruction.
The bill is part of the government's 2018-19 Budget measure to tighten tobacco border controls, and similar destruction powers already exist for other prohibited imports like psychoactive substances.
Empowers the Comptroller-General of Customs to cause seized tobacco products to be dealt with as they see fit, including immediate destruction.
Removes the current requirement to store seized prohibited imports for a minimum of 30 days before disposal.
Aligns tobacco products with existing controls for other prohibited imports such as psychoactive substances.
Australian Border Force officials and tobacco importers are affected by the bill.
